name: Crew Quarters
narrativeOnEnter: Four bunks, two occupied with personal effects. Lockers, a small desk, a mirror cracked at the corner. Personal items are scattered — whoever left did so quickly. One bunk has a data pad on the pillow.

action.text:
MERIDIAN STATION ALPHA — CREW IDENTIFICATION

Name: CHEN, YUKI
Role: Navigation Officer
Crew ID: #0447

Navigation override panel — Medical Bay.
Manual switch access code: B=ON, C=ON (A and D remain OFF).

Handwritten note on the back:
'Pod bay code — last four of mission stamp: 5519
DO NOT WRITE DOWN — but I always forget it.'

A personal photograph. Four crew members in orange jumpsuits, posing in front of an airlock. They're smiling.

Written on the back in blue ink:
'Meridian Alpha, Launch Day — Year 3'

One of them has a name tag: CHEN.

PERSONAL LOG — CHEN, YUKI

Entry 44:
'Station's been acting up for two days. Reactor deck is throwing warnings I've never seen before. Kovalev thinks it's a coolant calibration issue. He's gone down to check.

If this goes sideways:
— Engineering wiring schematic is taped inside the panel cover
— Reactor sequence is in the safety manual on Reactor Deck
— Cargo lock pattern is on the freight manifest in the Cargo Bay

Escape pod bay is stern lower deck. Code is on my ID tag. I keep forgetting.'

──
Entry 45 (next day):
'I was in the cargo bay checking the anomalous weight readings. Found a container we never logged. Seal was from a company called Δ Medical Dynamics. Inside: six devices. Compact. Medical-looking. Wire mounts — like they were designed to be attached to something permanent. Kovalev came in while I was looking. He went very quiet.

He said: I already know what those are.
He said: They're called Synaptic Response Recorders.
He said: There's one behind the vent panel in every crew quarters. Including mine. Including yours.
He said: They've been running since we launched. 63 days.

I asked him: Running what?
He didn't answer. He just said: I'm going to fix it.'

──
Entry 46 (last entry, handwriting shaky):
'Kovalev told me what he's going to do. I told him to stop. He won't.
He says the data in the buffer has to burn. That's the only way.
Maybe he's right. Maybe it doesn't matter if he's right.
The other ship is at 148.350 MHz — I found it on the cargo lading manifest, flagged by someone called CALLISTO.
If MERIDIAN-3 boards us: do not trust them.
Wait for the other one.
— Yuki Chen'

A regulation bunk, stripped down. Whoever slept here took their belongings. A sticky note is attached to the frame:

'Reactor sequence override code: ask Kovalev. He knows.'

On the floor beside the bunk, face-down: a second note, torn from a personal log.

'148.350 MHz — CALLISTO — transmit only after reactor is stable.
Do NOT signal MERIDIAN-3. Their charter is HELIOS GROUP.
Kovalev traced it: HELIOS GROUP = AXIOM.
The shuttle isn't rescue. It's extraction.
They're coming for the buffer data.
Don't let them dock.

CALLISTO has the Blackwood files. They know what AXIOM does with neural data.
They know about PROMETHEUS.
Contact them. They'll come in.'

A bunk with a rumpled sleep sack. A worn paperback book is wedged at the pillow end.

Inside the front cover: a name. 'KOVALEV, D.' And below it:

'Station callsign: MERIDIAN. The nav override panel in Med Bay runs on manual switches — biometric scanner has been offline since the power incident.'
